patterns.key_values: invoked-at-cursor radial menu / gesture HUD; chromeless (no traffic lights); frosted glass disc; center hub = deadzone + breadcrumb; item ring at ~0.70 radius
polar (radial) menu, ~9 items ~40deg apart; disclosure chevron = nested ring (submenu grammar in polar space); two item classes — expandable SF-Symbol wedges vs direct app-launch tiles

signature_moves: Fitts-optimal pie menu on macOS: polar layout puts every item the same short distance from the invoke point with large directional wedge targets, enabling learned one-gesture selection

Two item classes unified on one ring: monochrome SF-Symbol wedges that expand (chevron=nested ring) beside full-color app tiles that launch directly (no chevron) — taxonomy encoded in glyph treatment (Von Restorff)
Center hub is triple-duty: gesture deadzone (release=cancel) + focal anchor (only glowing element) + breadcrumb (labels the current ring)
defects: Contrast Dilution — 'Radial' center label pink-grey on near-white hub reads <4.5:1 (low-stakes passive title, but a real miss)
Selection/hover grammar unseen — cursor on Safari tile with no inset-rounded accent highlight; native selection binding unverified
HUD-over-content contrast is backdrop-dependent (inherent glass-HUD risk; fine over this bright wallpaper, untested on light/busy desktops)

aesthetic.direction: Apple-system Liquid-Glass HUD — leans on the platform's own material language rather than a committed bespoke direction; the boldness budget is spent entirely on the polar geometry, not on color or type

psychology: Fitts's Law — radial menu is the ideal case: constant short cursor-to-item distance + large angular wedge targets minimize acquisition time
Spatial memory / automaticity — fixed angular positions let users develop muscle-memory gestures ('flick up-right = folder'), delivering the 'one gesture' promise
Hick's Law + Progressive Disclosure — ~9 parallel-scannable items on the root ring; chevrons nest deeper actions instead of lengthening the ring
Von Restorff — monochrome glyphs vs full-color app tiles, and the lone glowing hub against the frosted field, make the differing elements the memorable ones
Aesthetic-Usability Effect — the Liquid-Glass polish buys perceived usability/trust on first contact
notes: Single surface from a marketing composite (cover.jpg, 1920x1080) — no captured screenshot, no chrome anchor, so scale is unknowable and all metrics are ratios/estimates at low confidence; reliable facts are scale-free ratios (hub 0.42 of disc, ring 0.70 radius). Radial/pie menu is not a stock AppKit control, but the MATERIAL grammar is genuinely native (Liquid-Glass edge-lensing, real SF Symbols, real superellipse app icons, chevron=submenu) — so this is a native app with a bespoke geometry, distinct from Alcove's iOS-transplant. Lineage-gate: material/glyph discipline may feed canon; the polar geometry may not (n=1 anyway). Liquid-Glass vs plain vibrancy not fully separable from one still (humility). The app icon (black superellipse, ring of 8 white capsule dashes depicting the menu) was NOT digested — Workflow A only — but noted for brand coherence with the dashed-ring motif. Contradiction watch: the app reads native by material yet uses zero standard AppKit controls (all custom-drawn) — treat as signature geometry, not a lineage downgrade.
